alignments.note: Subject noun keeps its own word.

Nominal predicate of a verbless clause takes the construction-supplied copula (rule 20) and the indefinite article that its nominal expression licenses (rule 15); discontinuous around 'everlasting' under rule 25.
One English word carries both the quantification and the lexeme of עוֹלָמִים, so the pair fuses under rule 30, headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme.

The temporal prepositional phrase predicates continuance of the subject 'thy dominion'; 'endureth' supplies its copular link under rule 20, not a separate lexical event. It joins בְּ with 'throughout' under rule 49, headed on the preposition.
First occurrence of the distributive repetition takes the English noun (rule 22).
The ASV writes no connective for the waw of the distributive repetition (rules 14 and 22).
Repeated occurrence rendered once by the ASV (rule 22).

review_notes: כָּל־עֹלָמִים is fused to 'everlasting' under rule 30; the competing reading marks כֹּל unrepresented beside עוֹלָמִים.
The ASV italic on 'endureth' does not make it added: temporal continuance is the copula of the written prepositional predicate (rules 7, 20 and 49).
